turns.en: So what I think is happening is a chest infection. That's why you've been coughing and feeling so tired. It's very common at this time of year.
turns.cy: Felly haint ar y frest sy'n digwydd, dw i'n meddwl. Dyna pam dach chi wedi bod yn pesychu ac yn teimlo mor flinedig. Mae o'n gyffredin iawn yr adeg yma o'r flwyddyn.
chunks: So what I think is happening is a chest infection
Felly haint ar y frest sy'n digwydd, dw i'n meddwl
English's pseudo-cleft relocates to a sy'-focus with the belief-clause pushed to the end — Welsh cannot stack 'what I think is … is'
That's why you've been coughing and feeling so tired
Dyna pam dach chi wedi bod yn pesychu ac yn teimlo mor flinedig
the yn must be restated on the second participle
It's very common at this time of year
Mae o'n gyffredin iawn yr adeg yma o'r flwyddyn

turns.en: Ah, right. That makes sense, I suppose.
turns.cy: A, iawn. Mae hynna'n gneud synnwyr, am wn i.
chunks: the same synnwyr frame as HG05's 'doesn't make sense'
the fixed am wn i, which uses the irregular short gwybod — English's verb has no Welsh reflex here

turns.en: The good news is it should clear completely with treatment. Most people feel a lot better within three or four days.
turns.cy: Y newyddion da ydy y dylai o glirio'n llwyr efo triniaeth. Mae'r rhan fwya o bobl yn teimlo lot yn well o fewn tri neu bedwar diwrnod.
chunks: The good news is it should clear completely with treatment
Y newyddion da ydy y dylai o glirio'n llwyr efo triniaeth
the identificatory ydy joining two clauses
Most people feel a lot better within three or four days
Mae'r rhan fwya o bobl yn teimlo lot yn well o fewn tri neu bedwar diwrnod
English's quantifier 'most' relocates to the noun phrase y rhan fwyaf o

turns.en: Three or four days. I can cope with that.
turns.cy: Tri neu bedwar diwrnod. Mi fedra i ymdopi efo hynny.
chunks: the numeral takes the singular in Welsh
Mi fedra i ymdopi efo hynny
ymdopi for 'cope', kept apart from dod i ben for 'manage'

turns.en: So here's the plan: a week of antibiotics, plenty of rest and fluids, and I want to hear from you if you're not clearly better by Friday.
turns.cy: Felly dyma'r cynllun: wythnos o wrthfiotigau, digon o orffwys a hylifau, a dw i isio clywed gynnoch chi os nad ydach chi'n amlwg well erbyn dydd Gwener.
chunks: a week of antibiotics, plenty of rest and fluids
wythnos o wrthfiotigau, digon o orffwys a hylifau
and I want to hear from you if you're not clearly better by Friday
a dw i isio clywed gynnoch chi os nad ydach chi'n amlwg well erbyn dydd Gwener
English's 'from you' relocates to the conjugated gynnoch chi — hearing is a gan-relation in Welsh

turns.en: Makes sense. What do I do if it's the weekend, though?
turns.cy: Gneud synnwyr. Ond be dw i'n neud os ydy hi'n benwythnos?
chunks: English's subject erases in the elliptical reply; the bare verbal noun stands
What do I do if it's the weekend, though?
Ond be dw i'n neud os ydy hi'n benwythnos?
English's clause-final 'though' fronts as ond, because Welsh has no postposed concessive

turns.en: What I think is happening is a chest infection - that's the cough and the tiredness.
turns.cy: Haint ar y frest sy'n digwydd, dw i'n meddwl — dyna'r peswch a'r blinder.
chunks: What I think is happening is a chest infection
Haint ar y frest sy'n digwydd, dw i'n meddwl
that's the cough and the tiredness

turns.en: Sorry, could you explain that again? What does that mean, exactly?
turns.cy: Sori, fedrwch chi esbonio hynny eto? Be'n union mae hynny'n ei olygu?
chunks: the conditional-as-request lands on the plain fedrwch chi — Welsh does not stack politeness here
Be'n union mae hynny'n ei olygu?
'exactly' fronts with the interrogative; the resumptive ei is obligatory

turns.en: Of course. There's an infection in the tubes of your lungs - a bug, basically. That's what's causing the cough and the tiredness. The tablets will kill the bug.
turns.cy: Wrth gwrs. Mae 'na haint yn nhiwbiau'ch ysgyfaint chi — chwilen, yn y bôn. Dyna sy'n achosi'r peswch a'r blinder. Mi wneith y tabledi ladd y chwilen.
chunks: There's an infection in the tubes of your lungs
Mae 'na haint yn nhiwbiau'ch ysgyfaint chi
the mae 'na existential; the nasal mutation after yn absorbed
the indefinite article erases; chwilen is the plain-speech bug, matching the doctor's own register shift
That's what's causing the cough and the tiredness
Dyna sy'n achosi'r peswch a'r blinder
the sy'-focus does English's cleft without any dummy
The tablets will kill the bug
Mi wneith y tabledi ladd y chwilen

turns.en: A bug in the tubes. Right. Now I understand you.
turns.cy: Chwilen yn y tiwbiau. Iawn. Rŵan dw i'n eich dallt chi.
chunks: kept apart from the ratifying 'Right' → Reit, which opens a move rather than accepting one
Rŵan dw i'n eich dallt chi

turns.en: That's it exactly. Does the rest make sense? What questions have you got for me?
turns.cy: Dyna fo'n union. Ydy'r gweddill yn gneud synnwyr? Pa gwestiynau sy gynnoch chi i mi?
chunks: What questions have you got for me?
Pa gwestiynau sy gynnoch chi i mi?
possession relocates to the sy' gan relative

turns.en: No questions. You've explained it lovely.
turns.cy: Dim cwestiynau. Dach chi wedi'i esbonio fo'n hyfryd.
chunks: Dach chi wedi'i esbonio fo'n hyfryd
the English dialect's bare adjective takes the Welsh adverbial yn, which the standard requires

turns.en: What I think is happening is a chest infection - common at this time of year.
turns.cy: Haint ar y frest sy'n digwydd, dw i'n meddwl — cyffredin yr adeg yma o'r flwyddyn.
chunks: What I think is happening is a chest infection
Haint ar y frest sy'n digwydd, dw i'n meddwl
common at this time of year
cyffredin yr adeg yma o'r flwyddyn

turns.en: So it's nothing to do with my heart, then? That's what I was really worried about.
turns.cy: Felly does 'na ddim byd i'w neud efo fy nghalon i, 'ta? Dyna be ro'n i wir yn poeni amdano fo.
chunks: So it's nothing to do with my heart, then?
Felly does 'na ddim byd i'w neud efo fy nghalon i, 'ta?
English's negative subject relocates to a negative existential; 'so' → felly and 'then' → 'ta stand side by side, each in its own role (S1)
That's what I was really worried about
Dyna be ro'n i wir yn poeni amdano fo

turns.en: Your heart is fine - I've listened to it, and it's strong and steady. This is the lungs. If I were worried, I would tell you straight.
turns.cy: Mae'ch calon chi'n iawn — dw i wedi gwrando arni hi, ac mae hi'n gry ac yn gyson. Yr ysgyfaint ydy hyn. Taswn i'n poeni, mi faswn i'n deud wrthach chi'n blaen.
chunks: dw i wedi gwrando arni hi
gwrando governs ar; calon is feminine, so arni hi
ac mae hi'n gry ac yn gyson
the yn must be restated on the second adjective
If I were worried, I would tell you straight
Taswn i'n poeni, mi faswn i'n deud wrthach chi'n blaen
the tas- conditional, which English marks with a past subjunctive

turns.en: You'd tell me straight. Good. That's all I ask, doctor.
turns.cy: Mi fasach chi'n deud wrtha i'n blaen. Da. Dyna'r cwbl dw i'n ei ofyn, doctor.
chunks: Mi fasach chi'n deud wrtha i'n blaen
the bare judgement, kept apart from the approving 'Good' → Da iawn that opens a nurse's move
Dyna'r cwbl dw i'n ei ofyn, doctor
the object relative with a resumptive ei

turns.en: Always. So - a week of antibiotics, rest, and fluids, and ring me if you're not better by Friday.
turns.cy: Bob amser. Felly — wythnos o wrthfiotigau, gorffwys a hylifau, a ffoniwch fi os nad ydach chi'n well erbyn dydd Gwener.
chunks: So - a week of antibiotics, rest, and fluids
Felly — wythnos o wrthfiotigau, gorffwys a hylifau
and ring me if you're not better by Friday
a ffoniwch fi os nad ydach chi'n well erbyn dydd Gwener
ffonio for telephoning, against canu for a bell

turns.en: Right. And what if it's the weekend?
turns.cy: Iawn. A be os ydy hi'n benwythnos?
chunks: And what if it's the weekend?
A be os ydy hi'n benwythnos?
